issues.legal_issue: A lease that creates a present demise is not an executory agreement frustrated merely because possession is to be delivered later and an intervening legal obstacle delays delivery.
material_facts: The registered lease created a demise in presenti and required the landlord to take steps to obtain and deliver possession to the lessee.
A prior occupant remained in possession, and rent-control laws temporarily impeded delivery of possession.
The landlord entered a later lease with the prior occupant while appeals concerning that occupant’s eviction were pending and then withdrew the appeals pursuant to a compromise.
By the time the matter was considered, the legal impediment to granting possession no longer applied.
issues.conclusion: The lease was not frustrated; it created an interest in the property, and the lessee was entitled to seek and obtain possession under it.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 105 of the Transfer of Property Act, delivery of possession is not a condition precedent to a lease taking effect where the instrument creates a demise in presenti. The characterization of an instrument as a lease rather than an agreement to lease is consistent with Narayan Chetty v. Muthaiah Servai, Sultanali Mulla Rassoji v. Tyeb Pir Mahomed, and Ramjoo Mahomed v. Haridas Mullick. The doctrine of frustration applies to executory contracts, not to a lease that has already created a present interest in the property.

predicates.appeal_from_dismissal_of_lease_based_pos: A lessee appeals the dismissal of a claim seeking possession under a lease.
predicates.present_demise_created: The lease instrument creates a present interest in the property rather than merely promising to grant a lease later.
predicates.possession_deferred_until_landlord_obtai: The lease provides for possession to be delivered after the landlord obtains it from an existing occupant.
predicates.temporary_legal_obstacle_to_delivery_has: A legal obstacle that had delayed delivery of possession no longer prevents the court from granting possession.

issues.definition: When a lessee appeals the dismissal of a possession claim, the instrument creates a present interest, possession was deferred until the landlord obtained it, and the temporary obstacle has ceased, the lessee is entitled to possession under the present demise.

issues.legal_issue: A court may assess entitlement to relief in light of the legal position existing when it decides the matter, rather than treating a legal impediment that has since ceased as permanently barring relief.
material_facts: Rent-control laws had impeded relief at earlier stages of the litigation.
A later rent-control law excluded buildings above a specified monthly rent from its coverage, and the rent for the premises exceeded that threshold.
The matter reached the Supreme Court after that change in the law.
issues.conclusion: The earlier rent-control impediment did not prevent the Court from granting relief on the basis of the current legal position.
issues.legal_principle: A court may take account of the present position and mould its relief accordingly, as held in Mohanlal Chunilal Kothari v. Tribhuvan Haribhai Tamboli. The Court applied Section 31 of the Mysore Rent Control Act, 1961, under which buildings with monthly rent exceeding the statutory threshold were outside the Act.

predicates.appeal_seeking_relief_delayed_by_legal_r: A party appeals seeking relief that had previously been impeded by a legal restriction.
predicates.current_legal_position_no_longer_imposes: The law in force when the court decides the matter no longer imposes the restriction that previously impeded relief.

issues.definition: If an appeal seeks relief previously impeded by a restriction that no longer applies under the current legal position, the court may mould relief to that current position.

issues.legal_issue: Where the lease makes possession the starting point of its term, the term begins on delivery of possession rather than on execution of the lease.
material_facts: The lease stated that rent would be payable from the date possession was handed over to the tenant.
The lease required the landlord to take steps to obtain and deliver possession as soon as possible.
The lease fixed an initial term and an option to extend it, but possession had not been delivered to the tenant.
issues.conclusion: The lease term had not begun to run from the date the lease was executed; it was to begin when possession was delivered, so the lease had not expired on the basis asserted.
issues.legal_principle: Section 110 of the Transfer of Property Act, which addresses when a lease commences, did not govern the case because the terms of the lease indicated that its term began on delivery of possession. The Court construed the lease provisions together, including the clause making rent payable from delivery and the clause setting the duration of the lease.

predicates.claim_for_possession_under_fixed_term_le: A party seeks possession under a lease that specifies a fixed term.
predicates.lease_makes_rent_payable_from_delivery_o: The lease provides that rent becomes payable when possession is delivered to the tenant.
predicates.landlord_is_required_to_obtain_and_deliv: The lease requires the landlord to obtain possession and deliver it to the tenant.
predicates.possession_not_delivered: The tenant has not received possession of the leased property.

issues.definition: When a possession claim concerns a fixed-term lease that makes rent payable on delivery, requires the landlord to obtain and deliver possession, and has not yet been acted on by delivery, the lease term begins on delivery of possession.
